principles.name: Hick's Law
principles.description: Decision time increases logarithmically with the number and complexity of choices. Reducing options and cognitive load speeds up user decisions.

actions.title: Reduce choice options
actions.description: Limit dropdown menus to 5-7 items max; use progressive disclosure for advanced options.

actions.title: Create visual hierarchy
actions.description: Use size, color, and spacing to guide attention to primary vs. secondary actions.

actions.title: Group related choices
actions.description: Organize options into logical categories (max 5 groups) to reduce scanning time.

uiPatterns: Sticky header bar for primary action in long scrolling pages
Summary/confirmation anchored at bottom of multi-step forms

principles.name: Miller's Law
principles.description: The average person can hold about 7 items (±2) in working memory. Organize information into chunks of 5-9 items for optimal recall.

actions.title: Chunk information
actions.description: Group related items into 5-9 item clusters with clear visual separation.

actions.title: Use progressive disclosure
actions.description: Show primary information first; reveal secondary details on demand.

actions.title: Provide memory aids
actions.description: Add tooltips, help text, and inline validation to reduce memory burden.

antiPatterns: Forms with >7 fields visible at once

principles.name: Von Restorff Effect
principles.description: When multiple similar objects are present, the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered.

actions.title: Highlight key elements
actions.description: Use color, size, or position to make critical actions and information stand out.

actions.title: Create visual contrast
actions.description: Make primary CTA buttons distinctly different from secondary actions.

actions.title: Isolate warnings
actions.description: Present error messages and alerts in visually distinct containers.

principles.name: Fitts's Law
principles.description: Time to reach a target is a function of its size and distance. Make critical interactive elements large and proximate.

actions.title: Increase target size
actions.description: Make buttons and touch targets at least 44x44px for easy clicking/tapping.

actions.title: Reduce distance
actions.description: Place related actions close together; anchor primary actions to screen edges.

actions.title: Use corner placement
actions.description: Position important controls at screen corners where they have infinite width.

antiPatterns: Centered primary actions on large screens

principles.name: Serial Position Effect
principles.description: Users tend to remember the first (primacy) and last (recency) items in a list better than middle items.

actions.title: Position key items first
actions.description: Place the most important navigation items at the beginning of menus.

actions.title: Use recency for CTAs
actions.description: Position critical calls-to-action at the end of forms and lists.

actions.title: Limit list length
actions.description: Keep lists under 7 items or use categorization to break up longer lists.

antiPatterns: Burying important items in middle of lists
uiPatterns: Step indicators at top of multi-step processes
Summary panels at the end of forms
Recently used items at top of lists

principles.name: Jakob's Law
principles.description: Users spend most of their time on other sites. They prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know.

actions.title: Use standard patterns
actions.description: Follow established UI conventions: hamburger menu for navigation, magnifying glass for search.

actions.title: Maintain consistency
actions.description: Keep navigation, layout, and interaction patterns consistent across your product.

actions.title: Match user mental models
actions.description: Design based on how users expect things to work, not how you think they should work.

principles.name: Peak-End Rule
principles.description: People judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak (most intense point) and at its end, rather than the total sum or average of every moment.

actions.title: Design for moments
actions.description: Create memorable positive peaks during key interactions (completion, discovery).

actions.title: End on a high note
actions.description: Ensure final steps (confirmation, success messages) are delightful and reassuring.

actions.title: Minimize negative peaks
actions.description: Prevent intense frustration points; spread out necessary friction.

uiPatterns: Clear success states with next steps

principles.name: Progressive Disclosure
principles.description: Show only the essential information first and progressively reveal more complex options as users need them or demonstrate competence.

actions.title: Start simple
actions.description: Present only core functionality initially; hide advanced options behind expandable sections.

actions.title: Use smart defaults
actions.description: Pre-fill forms with intelligent defaults that work for most users.

actions.title: Reveal progressively
actions.description: Show additional fields/ options only when previous selections require them.

antiPatterns: Advanced settings mixed with basic options

principles.name: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
principles.description: Users perceive more aesthetically pleasing designs as more usable and are more tolerant of minor usability issues when the design is beautiful.

actions.title: Invest in visual polish
actions.description: Use consistent spacing, typography, and color palettes to create a professional appearance.

actions.title: Maintain consistency
actions.description: Ensure visual elements align with your brand and create harmony across the interface.

actions.title: Use quality imagery
actions.description: High-quality photos and icons elevate perceived value and trustworthiness.

principles.name: Doherty Threshold
principles.description: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures neither has to wait on the other.

actions.title: Optimize response times
actions.description: Aim for <400ms response time for all user interactions to maintain flow state.

actions.title: Provide immediate feedback
actions.description: Show loading states, skeleton screens, or progress indicators during longer operations.

actions.title: Preload content
actions.description: Anticipate user needs and prefetch data before it's requested.

principles.name: Goal-Gradient Effect
principles.description: The tendency to approach a goal increases with proximity to the goal. Users are more motivated as they get closer to completion.

actions.title: Show progress
actions.description: Display completion percentages and progress bars to motivate users to finish.

actions.title: Break into stages
actions.description: Divide long processes into smaller milestones to create multiple goal gradients.

actions.title: Celebrate progress
actions.description: Acknowledge achievements at intervals to maintain motivation.

antiPatterns: Long forms without breaks or milestones

principles.name: Social Proof
principles.description: People look to others' behavior to guide their own, especially in uncertain situations. Displaying social validation reduces anxiety and increases confidence.

actions.title: Show user counts
actions.description: Display how many users have taken an action (downloads, purchases, signups).

actions.title: Include testimonials
actions.description: Feature reviews, ratings, and testimonials from satisfied users.

actions.title: Highlight activity
actions.description: Show real-time activity (recent purchases, current viewers) to demonstrate popularity.
